afOutro: Tip: the "no signup, no watermark" part matters more than the prompt wording — most tools that accept these prompts put a watermark on the free result.
faq1a: Yes. It runs on Cloudflare Workers AI with a free daily quota. Normal use won't hit limits.
faq6q: Is this an AI action figure generator?
faq6a: Yes. The Action figure preset renders you as a collectible figure in blister packaging, and the Doll preset renders a soft-vinyl doll. Both work from a photo — you don't have to write a prompt.
faq7q: Is the result a real 3D model?
faq7a: No. You get a high-resolution image rendered in a 3D figurine style — not an .obj or .stl file you can print. Think of it as a preview of the figure, made for sharing or mockups.
faq2a: No. Your photo is processed in memory and discarded immediately after the result is generated. Nothing is stored.
faq3q: What kind of photo works best?
faq3a: Front-facing portraits with clear lighting and a plain background work best. For Action figure or Doll, a full-body or half-body shot gives a better result than a tight face crop. Avoid blurry, low-light, or heavily filtered images.
faq4a: The AI model has a content filter that occasionally misidentifies harmless images. If generation fails, try a different photo with a simpler background.
faq5q: Can I use the result commercially?
faq5a: Yes. The tool doesn't add watermarks. You own the result, but make sure you have the rights to the original photo.
faq8q: Can I turn my figure into a real physical figurine?
faq8a: Yes — the image is the design, and one extra step gets you a 3D-printed figure. See the full workflow and costs in the 3D printing guide.
